value.rationale: The right Peirce spectrum is an established invariant of quandle algebras, and the immediately preceding odd-order theorem leaves the even cases untreated. The complete all-finite-abelian classification gives a sharp structural boundary: elementary-two cores have {1}, groups with nontrivial odd torsion but no fourth-order torsion have the discrete {0,+/-1}, and a single C4 subgroup yields all complex values. Thus non-Latinity alone does not predict spectral size. This is an infinite-family classification, not a fixed-table recomputation.
